title: 1998 AHSME Problem 29
statement: A point \((x,y)\) in the plane is called a lattice point if both \(x\) and \(y\) are integers. The area of the largest square that contains exactly three lattice points in its interior is closest to

solutions.text: It suffices to enclose the three noncollinear lattice points \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0).\) In a maximal placement, two opposite sides are pinned by neighboring lattice points; the greatest possible separation is the distance \(\sqrt5\) between parallel lines through \((1,1)\) and \((0,-1).\) Hence the area is at most \(5.\) This is attained by the square bounded by \[ \begin{aligned} y&=2x+2,\\ y&=2x-3,\\ 2y+x&=3,\\ 2y+x&=-2. \end{aligned} \] Its area is \(5\) and exactly the three stated lattice points lie inside. Thus D is correct.
